info.title: RedChirp External REST API
info.description:
# Introduction

The RedChirp REST API is available free of charge to all RedChirp users.  

# Sandbox accounts

If you are interested in developing an integration for RedChirp but do not yet
have a RedChirp account, contact help@redchirp.com.

# Creating an API key

You can create / revoke API keys using the RedChirp GUI.  To do so:

1. Sign into RedChirp

2. Navigate to the Main Menu

3. Search for "API Keys"

4. Click "Settings > API Keys"

5. Use the search bar's action menu to create "New Credentials..."

6. The RedChirp REST API uses HTTP basic authentication.  The username will
be the Credential Id shown in the API keys table, the password is the secret
that you entered into the Create New API Key Dialog

# Authentication

There are two ways to authenticate with the API: API keys and app-based authentication.

**API Keys**

API keys are quick and convenient for testing or when you only need to access data for a single organization.  You should not use API keys to access data from multiple organizations, as excessive cross-organization requests from the same IP address may be blocked. For multi-organization scenarios, always use app-based authentication instead.

**App Based Authentication**

App-based authentication is recommended for any integration that will be used by multiple organizations.

**Authentication Details**

API calls are authenticated using HTTP basic authentication.  The username is credential id (case insensitive) and the secret (case sensitive) is the secret you entered when creating the API key.  

Per the HTTP specification this means that your HTTP request must have an `Authentication` header, the value of which should be the Base64 encoding of the string `your_credentials_id:your_secret`

For example, if your credeintial id was `a052871f-44f2-45d6-a63d-4ba5b2a3d634` and your secret was `12345`, then the Authenication header would be `YTA1Mjg3MWYtNDRmMi00NWQ2LWE2M2QtNGJhNWIyYTNkNjM0OjEyMzQ1` -- which is the Base64 encoding of the string `a052871f-44f2-45d6-a63d-4ba5b2a3d634:12345`

If you need help Base64 encoding a string, you can use this [web utility](https://www.base64encode.org/) or, from the command line `echo -n 'the string you want to encode here' | base64`

# Rate Limits

By default, API calls are rate limited at a rate of 15 requests per second. 
If you need higher limits, please contact help@redchirp.com

# Pagination

Endpoints that list objects (e.g. /api/v1/external/{organization_id}/employee-account) accept an *optional* query string parameter, `page_size`, that allows you to control how many objects will be returned per page (the default page size is 240 objects).  If there are more than one page of results, then links object will contain a field, `next_page`.  The `next_page` value will be the fully qualified url for the next page of results.  

# Data Ingress API

If you are looking to build an API that RedChirp can integrate with (for example: to integrate a CRM system with RedChirp), check out the [Example Data Ingress API Documentation](https://app.swaggerhub.com/apis-docs/RedChirp/red-chirp-example-data-ingress-api/1.0.0)

put.description:
Record a consent event in your organization's consent register.

**Note**: By default, this endpoint does **not require authentication**. It is designed to log consent events from clients. Since the endpoint does not expose or allow access to any sensitive data (the endpoint is receive only -- data is posted to it but no sensitive information is returned), many organization's take the view that there is no need to include authentication tokens in requests to this endpoint.

Some support for this approach may be found within NIST guidance that authentication requirements should be appropriate to the data and risk level, and that organizations may implement less stringent controls for receive only endpoints handling only non-sensitive information, especially when privacy and usability are prioritized (NIST SP 800-63, NIST SP 800-204, NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0).

Organization's may request that access to this endpoint be rejected if they are absent a valid API authorization token. Once this election is implemented any future call to this endpoint from any source will be rejected unless it has a valid API authorization token. It will then be the electing organization's responsibility to ensure the API is used in such a way that the API secret is not disclosed -- generally this means that you will no longer be able to access this endpoint from front end code directly.

get.description: List conversation summaries.  A conversation summary is the latest, point-in-time snapshot of an active conversation between your organization and an recipient (e.g. a customer, candidate, or employee).  Analogous to the "at-a-glance" previews displayed on a mobile device's native messaging application, a conversation summary allows a user to quickly see summary information of a conversation in progress. This allows frontend interfaces to efficiently render sorted conversation lists without fetching exhaustive message logs.

put.description:
Immediately sends a double opt-in message to the specified recipient. This message prompts the recipient to reply “YES” to confirm their consent to receive future communications. Until the recipient responds with “YES,” they are treated as opted out and will not receive additional messages.

Because this message is sent immediately (potentially at an inconvenient time, such as outside normal business hours), this endpoint should only be used when the recipient has taken a clear action indicating intent to opt in (for example, submitting a form requesting messaging enrollment).

If no message content is provided, a default double opt-in message will be used. However, it is strongly recommended to customize the message to include relevant context so the recipient understands why they are receiving the request.

parameters.name: organization_id
parameters.description: Your organization id

requestBody.description: The parameters for the double opt-in message

from.description: The RedChirp phone number that the double opt-in message should be sent from.  A wide variety of formats are accepted, including E164 (e.g. +12737879143) and ###-###-#### (e.g. 273-787-9143)

to.description: The phone number of the intended recipient.  A wide variety of formats are accepted, including E164 (e.g. +12737879143) and ###-###-#### (e.g. 273-787-9143)

message.description: The double opt-in message to be sent.  If not specified, then the organization's default double opt-in message will be sent

send_if_promotional_consent_already_on_f.description: Send the message if promotional consent is already on file (defaults to false)

description_recipient_action_that_trigge.description: Describe the specific action taken by the recipient that triggered this message. For example: the recipient completed a form (include the form URL), or the recipient indicated they would like to receive text messages during a phone call with a team member.

200.description: No double opt-in message was sent because the recipient was already opted-in to promotional messaging
